::: {.lede}
I work across the whole data workflow: turning messy data into clean pipelines, building R packages and Shiny apps, writing reproducible reports, and teaching other people to do the same.

Most of that work has been in air quality and environmental analytics. At WSP (formerly Ricardo) I build reporting, tooling and training for UK government clients, and I'm a core maintainer of the [openair](https://openair-project.github.io/openair/) family of open-source R packages. Before that I did a PhD at the University of York, building statistical models from hundreds of thousands of real-world vehicle measurements.
:::

## What I do

::: {.skills}
- **R package development.** I maintain `{openair}`, `{openairmaps}`, `{worldmet}` and `{deweather}`, and led the move of `{openair}` from lattice to ggplot2 in version 3.0. I also wrote `{ukaq}`, `{euroaq}` and `{leaf.magic}`, and I've had features merged into open source projects like `{leaflet}`, `{dygraphs}` and `{prismatic}`.

- **Reproducible reporting.** Quarto reports that go from raw monitoring data to published output, including annual network reports for Defra.

- **Data visualisation.** Static and interactive graphics with ggplot2, plotnine, leaflet, gt and Observable. Runner-up and honourable mention in the Posit Table Contest.

- **Shiny apps.** Dashboards and internal tools for clients and colleagues.

- **Teaching.** Posit Certified Tidyverse Instructor. I've taught R to analysts from Defra, the Environment Agency, UKHSA, UKCEH and CASANZ.
:::
